what_was_proven.claim: Atomic double-entry: every ledger posting is exactly one DEBIT + one CREDIT, never a half-posting.
what_was_proven.evidence: Whole-table scan after all scenarios: 82,663 distinct txIds, 165,326 ENTRY items = exactly 2 per txId; 82,663 healthy {DEBIT,CREDIT} pairs; 0 orphaned legs, 0 malformed pairs (docs/load/raw/ledger-integrity-final.json). Asserted from data, not from an error counter.

what_was_proven.claim: Conservation of money (synchronous/internal path): transfers move money between accounts, never create or destroy it.
what_was_proven.evidence: S1 both subsections: whole-table sum(balanceCents) = 0 before and after (delta 0); 0 accounts negative. Closed system across all 208 accounts (docs/load/raw/s1-*-before.json / *-after.json).

what_was_proven.claim: Conservation of money (asynchronous/external path): money parked in the clearing account at accept-time always leaves it — to SPI_SETTLED on settlement OR back to the payer on reversal — never stranded. BOTH branches proven.
what_was_proven.evidence: Settlement branch (S5, no fault injection): 515 external sends all reached SETTLED; SPI_CLEARING 0->0; SPI_SETTLED delta 515,000c = 515 x 1,000c; 0 orphaned. Reversal branch (S5b, mock-bacen reject-keys + failure-rate 0.2): 541 accepted -> 271 SETTLED + 270 REVERSED, 0 in flight; SPI_CLEARING returned to 0; SPI_SETTLED delta 271,000c = settled x 1,000c only (reversals do not credit SPI_SETTLED); whole-table sum delta 0; and PER TRANSACTION, all 270 reversals credited the EXACT original amount back to their OWN payer (270/270 verified, 0 mismatches) via a complete debit-clearing/credit-payer pair (docs/load/raw/s5b-result.json, docs/load/raw/s5b-reversal-pertx.json).

what_was_proven.claim: Non-negative balance under contention: the ledger's balance guard, inside the TransactWriteItems, stops overdraft exactly at the funded amount.
what_was_proven.evidence: S1 balance-guard: acc-lt-s1bal funded for exactly 10 sends at 10,000c each settled exactly 10 under a 50-VU storm; 11,586 further attempts refused INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS; 0 negative balances observed (docs/load/raw/s1-result.json).

what_was_proven.claim: Daily-limit reservation is exact and leak-free: settled x amount never exceeds the limit, and no reservation is lost.
what_was_proven.evidence: S1 limit-guard on a FRESHLY reseeded alice (counter absent): settled exactly 50 = 500,000c / 10,000c; alice's LIMIT#acc-001/DAY#2026-08-17 counter read 500,000c afterward (= 50 x 10,000c). This resolves the prior run's 49 as leftover same-day usage, NOT a reservation leak (see verdict.limit_guard_49_vs_50).

what_was_proven.claim: Idempotency under a retry storm: exactly one real ledger posting per business operation, however many clients race the same key.
what_was_proven.evidence: S3: 30 VUs racing one Idempotency-Key per round x 20 rounds -> 20 real postings (one per round), 580 byte-identical replays, 29 in-progress 409s, 0 rounds with no winner, 0 double postings on winners (docs/load/raw/s3-result.json).

limit_guard_49_vs_50.decision_rule: limit-guard settling 50 confirms the prior run's 49 was leftover same-day usage. Settling 49 again on a freshly reseeded environment rules that out and makes a reservation leak the leading hypothesis - investigate before any of these numbers are published.
limit_guard_49_vs_50.outcome: Settled 50 on the freshly reseeded environment, with alice's daily-limit counter confirmed ABSENT before the run. Per the rule, this confirms the prior 49 was leftover same-day consumption (a request against alice earlier that same calendar day), NOT a reservation leak. Corroborated by the code review in RESULTS.md (the reserve is a single conditional UpdateItem with no read-then-write race; the prior run's counter state that would have proven it directly was already gone before the audit - see EXPECTATIONS.md's limitation note).

fix_applied.summary: DynamoDB moved out of LocalStack into a standalone amazon/dynamodb-local container (infra/docker-compose.yml), reachable at a separate property (AwsProperties#dynamoDbEndpointUrl) than SNS/SQS (which stay on LocalStack). Root cause and diagnostic ladder: docs/load/BOTTLENECK.md.
fix_applied.root_cause: LocalStack's own DynamoDB support proxies every call through an internal Python HTTP client (a plain requests.Session, via rolo's SimpleRequestsClient) to the same DynamoDBLocal.jar this fix runs directly -- but that internal proxy has a fixed, non-configurable connection-pool cap (requests' library default, pool_maxsize=10) that became the throughput ceiling under load.
fix_applied.app_throughput_before_after: ~8.5-8.9 req/s -> ~150-172 req/s (S2, this pass) -- roughly a 19x improvement, comfortably clearing the >=100 req/s target.

outbox_publisher_backlog.finding: The outbox polling publisher (payment-service, default batch-size 25 per 1s tick => ~25/s) cannot keep pace with sustained internal-send throughput (~150 req/s in S2). After S0-S3 the sparse gsi3 held 55,538 unpublished PixSettled events; at 25/s that is ~37 minutes to drain at rest.
outbox_publisher_backlog.correctness_impact: None on money-safety: at-least-once publish-then-mark on the sparse GSI loses nothing, and the internal PixSettled events match no existing subscription (settlement-queue filters eventType=PixDebited), so they fan out to SNS and go nowhere until Sprint 8/10 queues exist. The impact is latency: an external PixDebited event queued behind the backlog stays DEBITED long enough to cross the 120s stuck threshold and be REVERSED by reconciliation instead of settling (observed on a pre-S5 smoke send).
outbox_publisher_backlog.s5_mitigation: For S5 the batch was bumped to 800 (infra/docker-compose.s5.yml) to drain the backlog in ~2 min, and BACEN settlement latency lowered to 100ms via /admin/config so the single-threaded settlement consumer kept pace; both restored to defaults after S5. This is a documented load-test-only knob, like the fraud loadtest profile - it changes throughput, not correctness.
outbox_publisher_backlog.production_note: In production the publisher batch/tick and a multi-instance settlement consumer would be sized to the send rate; the single-process, single-consumer local stack is the constraint, not the design.

trimming_rule.headline_policy: Raw is the headline figure everywhere; trimmed is a clearly-labelled secondary, diagnostic view. The ~31s stalls are real server-side latency (docs/load/BOTTLENECK.md RUNG 4, confirmed from application log timestamps), not a measurement artifact, so they are not 'corrected' away.
trimming_rule.status_this_run: removed_rate stayed in a 0-4% band across S0/S1/S2/S3 (S5 sends were not latency-analyzed - its claim is conservation, not latency). A 0-4% removed rate means 0-4% of requests genuinely took ~31s, so raw p99 is ~31s at almost every stage; the platform's <2s p99 send target is not met under this environment stall, and that is reported plainly rather than hidden behind the trimmed figure.

environment_limitation.summary: Real, periodic multi-second (~31s) stalls inside whichever process is serving DynamoDB under load (docs/load/BOTTLENECK.md RUNG 4, confirmed from the application's own server-side log timestamps, not just client timing) are present at ~1% even at 1 VU (S0). A stalled request still succeeds (same 202 Accepted, ~31s late) - money safety is unaffected, but the <2s p99 send target is blown on the affected requests.
environment_limitation.portability: The SHAPE (flat throughput ceiling, Little's-Law-consistent queueing, zero real errors past 100 req/s, and every money invariant holding) is a real, reproducible property of this codebase. The ABSOLUTE ~150-172 req/s ceiling and the ~31s stall are specific to single-process dynamodb-local on this WSL2/Docker-Desktop machine and would differ against real AWS DynamoDB.

caveats: dynamodb-local (the standalone container) is still a single-process DynamoDB Local instance, not real AWS DynamoDB.

settlement-service runs a SINGLE-THREADED sequential SQS consumer (batch 5), so with BACEN's default 2s latency it settles only ~0.5/s; S5 lowered BACEN latency to keep the pipeline ahead of its 120s stuck threshold. This is a local-stack sizing constraint, not a design limit.
Only 2 of the 208 seeded accounts (alice/acc-001, bob/acc-002) are 'real' fixtures; the other 206 are load-test-only ring/exhaustible accounts from tools/k6/seed/seed-load-test-fixtures.sh.
fraud-service has no runtime latency/failure-injection knob -- s4_fraud did not run; see docs/steps/step-64.md (proposed, unimplemented).
S1 ran under the fraud-service `loadtest` Spring profile (velocity thresholds only raised); S0/S2/S3/S5 ran on the default fraud profile. See RESULTS.md 'Fraud scoring under load'.
This is WSL2 on Windows (Docker Desktop backend), not bare-metal Linux.
S2's fraud_denied_rate is a fixture artifact (ring-account concentration vs throughput), not a capacity signal.

ledger_integrity_whole_table.method: full scan of pix_ledger ENTRY items, grouped by txId (gsi1pk = TX#<txId>), leg count + direction multiset per group
ledger_integrity_whole_table.query: scan pix_transactions is NOT this; this is scan pix_ledger where begins_with(sk,'ENTRY#') projecting txId+direction, then group_by txId and assert each group is exactly {DEBIT,CREDIT}

s5_async_conservation.settlement_conditions: BACEN latency 100ms (via /admin/config); outbox batch 800 (infra/docker-compose.s5.yml); BACEN failure-rate/timeout-rate at 0.0 defaults (no reversal injection) - both knobs restored after
s5_async_conservation.note: SETTLEMENT branch only — failure/timeout injection was 0.0, so 0 reversals. The reversal branch is proven by s5b below.

s5b_async_conservation_with_reversals.purpose: Exercise the REVERSAL branch of the async conservation claim, which s5 left unproven (money BACK TO THE PAYER on reversal, never stranded).
s5b_async_conservation_with_reversals.reversal_trigger_finding: Established from the code before running: reject-keys is the ONLY send-reachable reversal trigger (creditor key refused -> settlement recorded FAILED -> HTTP 422 -> SpiSettlementRejectedException -> finalizer.reverse -> <txId>-rev posting debit clearing / credit payer). failure-rate (503) and timeout both map to SpiCallFailedException = UNKNOWN -> retry (a timeout resolves to SETTLED via query-before-retry), NEITHER reverses. So failure-rate 0.2 alone cannot make a reversal happen; reject-keys drives the reversals and failure-rate 0.2 additionally exercises the transient-retry path.
s5b_async_conservation_with_reversals.accounts: senders: 200-account ring; destinations: bob@otherbank.com (SETTLED) / carol@otherbank.com (REVERSED, in reject-keys)
s5b_async_conservation_with_reversals.injection: mock-bacen reject-keys=[carol@otherbank.com], failure-rate=0.2, timeout-rate=0 (timeout resolves to SETTLED not REVERSED, and at a 15s hang on the single-threaded consumer would swamp the run), BACEN latency 100ms, outbox batch 800 — all restored after

per_transaction_reversal_check.method: for every REVERSED txId, join its tx META (debtorAccountId, amountCents) against its <txId>-rev ledger posting; assert the CREDIT leg goes to the ORIGINAL payer for the EXACT original amount and the DEBIT leg is SPI_CLEARING for -amount. Asserted per transaction, not on an aggregate (equal-and-opposite errors across two accounts would cancel in a total).
